arxiv-2111-01310.title: Log adjunction: moduli part
arxiv-2111-01310.creator: V.V. Shokurov
arxiv-2111-01310.description: Abstract Upper moduli part of adjunction is introduced and its basic property are discussed. The moduli part satisfies the BP in the case of rational multiplicities and is nef in the maximal case. Usually we assume that the base field k is algebraicaly closed of characteristic 0 , e.g., k=\mathbb{C} . We start from the divisorial part. Definition 1 .

arxiv-2203-09473.title: Product manifolds as realisations of general linear symmetries
arxiv-2203-09473.creator: Tom Lawrence
arxiv-2203-09473.description: Abstract This paper considers the relationship between geometry, symmetry and fundamental interactions - gravity and those mediated by gauge fields. We explore product spacetimes which a) have the necessary symmetries for gauge interactions and four-dimensional gravity and b) reduce to an N N -dimensional isotropic universe in their flat space limit.

arxiv-2211-10760.title: Evaluating Synthetic Tabular Data Generated To Augment Small Sample Datasets
arxiv-2211-10760.creator: Javier Marín
arxiv-2211-10760.description: Abstract This work proposes a method to evaluate synthetic tabular data generated to augment small sample datasets. While data augmentation techniques can increase sample counts for machine learning applications, traditional validation approaches fail when applied to extremely limited sample sizes.

arxiv-2308-10064.title: Efficient Representation Learning for Healthcare with Cross-Architectural Self-Supervision
arxiv-2308-10064.creator: Pranav Singh, Jacopo Cirrone
arxiv-2308-10064.description: Abstract In healthcare and biomedical applications, extreme computational requirements pose a significant barrier to adopting representation learning. Representation learning can enhance the performance of deep learning architectures by learning useful priors from limited medical data. However, state-of-the-art self-supervised techniques suffer from reduced performance when using smaller batch sizes or shorter pretraining epochs, which are more practical in clinical settings.

arxiv-2401-07242.title: Testing Sumsets is Hard
arxiv-2401-07242.creator: Xi Chen, Shivam Nadimpalli, Tim Randolph, Rocco A. Servedio, Or Zamir
arxiv-2401-07242.description: Abstract A subset S S of the Boolean hypercube 𝔽 2 n \mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} is a sumset if S = { a + b : a , b ∈ A } S=\{a+b\mathrel{\mathop{\mathchar 58\relax}}a,b\in A\} for some A ⊆ 𝔽 2 n A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n} . Sumsets are central objects of study in additive combinatorics, featuring in several influential results.

arxiv-2410-18648.title: GADT: Enhancing Transferable Adversarial Attacks through Gradient-guided Adversarial Data Transformation
arxiv-2410-18648.creator: Yating Ma, Xiaogang Xu, Liming Fang, Zhe Liu
arxiv-2410-18648.description: Abstract Current Transferable Adversarial Examples (TAE) are primarily generated by adding Adversarial Noise (AN). Recent studies emphasize the importance of optimizing Data Augmentation (DA) parameters along with AN, which poses a greater threat to real-world AI applications. However, existing DA-based strategies often struggle to find optimal solutions due to the challenging DA search procedure without proper guidance.

arxiv-2411-14616.title: Coupled dynamics of wall pressure and transpiration, with implications for the modeling of tailored surfaces and turbulent drag reduction
arxiv-2411-14616.creator: Simon Toedtli 1, Anthony Leonard 2, Beverley McKeon 3
arxiv-2411-14616.description: Abstract Wall-based active and passive flow control for drag reduction in low Reynolds number ( Re \mathrm{Re} ) turbulent flows can lead to three typical phenomena: i) attenuation or ii) amplification of the near-wall cycle, and iii) generation of spanwise rollers.

arxiv-2503-19062.title: Color Transfer with Modulated Flows
arxiv-2503-19062.creator: Maria Larchenko, Alexander Lobashev, Dmitry Guskov, Vladimir Vladimirovich Palyulin
arxiv-2503-19062.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce Modulated Flows (ModFlows), a novel approach for color transfer between images based on rectified flows. The primary goal of the color transfer is to adjust the colors of a target image to match the color distribution of a reference image.

arxiv-2506-11795.title: Ultra-Slow-Roll Inflation on the Lattice II: Nonperturbative Curvature Perturbation
arxiv-2506-11795.creator: Angelo Caravano, Gabriele Franciolini, Sébastien Renaux-Petel
arxiv-2506-11795.description: Abstract Building on the recent lattice simulations of ultra-slow-roll (USR) dynamics presented in Caravano et al. 2024a , we investigate the role of the nonlinear relation between the inflaton field configuration and the curvature perturbation ζ \zeta , the key observable after inflation.

arxiv-2511-00205.creator: Yuhan Deng, Akshay Srivatsan, Sebastian Ingino, Francis Chua, Yasmine Mitchell, Matthew Vilaysack, Keith Winstein
arxiv-2511-00205.description: Abstract . We describe a system for serverless computing where users, programs, and the underlying platform share a common representation of a computation: a deterministic procedure, run in an environment of well-specified data or the outputs of other computations. This representation externalizes I/O: data movement over the network is performed exclusively by the platform.

arxiv-2605-27268.creator: Samer Awad, Javier Conde, Carlos Arriaga, Tairan Fu, Javier Coronado-Blázquez, Pedro Reviriego

pmc-10570974.title: Chest wall depression caused by tissue expander use in breast reconstruction with recoiling following expander removal: a case report
pmc-10570974.creator: Jong-Ho Kim, Se Yeon Lee, Chan Yeong Heo
pmc-10570974.description: BackgroundWhile the number of implant-based immediate breast reconstructions has increased, two-stage reconstructions still comprise a significant proportion. Some studies have reported chest wall depression (CWD) following tissue expander insertion; however, there have been no reports on chest wall recoiling following expander removal.

pmc-10655295.title: WGX50 mitigates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity through inhibition of mitochondrial ROS and ferroptosis
pmc-10655295.creator: Panpan Tai, Xinyu Chen, Guihua Jia, Guanjun Chen, Lian Gong, Yaxin Cheng, Zhuan Li, Heng Wang, Aiyan Chen, Ganghua Zhang, Yuxing Zhu, Mengqing Xiao, Zhanwang Wang, Yunqing Liu, Dongyong Shan, Dong He, Moying Li, Tianzuo Zhan, Abbas Khan, Xiaohui Li, Xiangxiang Zeng, Chaopeng Li, Dongsheng Ouyang, Ke
pmc-10655295.description: BackgroundDoxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) is a major impediment to its clinical application. It is indispensable to explore alternative treatment molecules or drugs for mitigating DIC. WGX50, an organic extract derived from Zanthoxylum bungeanum Maxim, has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant biological activity, however, its function and mechanism in DIC remain unclear.MethodsWe established DOX-induced cardiotoxicity models both in vitro and in vivo.

pmc-11342811.title: Literature review and case study of recurrent EPGA with elevated IgG4 and positive HBsAg successfully treated with rituximab
pmc-11342811.creator: Junru Wang, Jun Wang, Nan Wang, Wei Wang, Ping Zhang, Yingying Lin, Guisen Li, Yurong Zou, Xiang Zhong
pmc-11342811.description: BackgroundEosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare form of autoimmune vasculitis. The involvement of IgG4 and HBsAg in EGPA is less common but can occur and may present unique challenges in management.Case presentation:We present a case study of a 70-year-old female diagnosed with EGPA confirmed via renal biopsy.

pmc-11402959.title: Associations of head and neck cancers with herpes zoster in the preceding five years
pmc-11402959.creator: Chao-Hung Chen, Sudha Xirasagar, Shih-Han Hung, Herng-Ching Lin, Chin-Shyan Chen
pmc-11402959.description: This population-based study investigated the risk of having had prior herpes zoster within five years preceding a diagnosis of head and neck cancer. We conducted a case-control study that included 9,191 patients with a diagnosis of head and neck cancer in Taiwan’s Longitudinal Health Insurance Database 2010 and 36,764 matched controls.

pmc-11509180.title: Factors Associated with Postoperative Complications After Congenital Duodenal Obstruction Surgery: A Retrospective Study
pmc-11509180.creator: Andreea Moga, Radu Bălănescu, Laura Bălănescu, Patricia Cîmpeanu, Mircea Andriescu, Mirela Elena Vasile, Ruxandra Caragata, Ralph Fingerhut
pmc-11509180.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and Objectives: Duodenal atresia and stenosis are common causes of intestinal obstruction. Associated anomalies significantly influence early postoperative mortality, while postoperative complications impact long-term survival. Materials and Methods: Over a 13-year period from January 2010 to August 2023, a total of 74 infants and children with congenital duodenal obstruction were treated at “Grigore Alexandrescu” Children’s Emergency Hospital and met the inclusion criteria. All patients diagnosed with duodenal obstruction (both instrinsic and extrinsic causes) were included.

pmc-12554394.creator: Lauren A Eberly, Kaitlyn Shultz, Sanjay Kishore, Margaret Hayden, Sarah Turecamo, Howard M Julien, Emily Niklaus Davis, Ashwin Nathan, Sameed Ahmed M Khatana
pmc-12554394.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIncarcerated individuals have a disproportionate burden of cardiovascular risk factors. pmc-12636892.title: CD28 signaling complexes are correlated with patient outcomes in anti-CD19 41BB-costimulation CAR T cell therapy
pmc-12636892.creator: Isabella H Draper, William Selke, Samuel A Ritmeester-Loy, Felicia Harsh, Colleen Annesley, Corinne Summers, Rebecca Gardner, Wooyoung Kim, Stephen EP Smith
pmc-12636892.description: BackgroundChimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells targeting CD19 achieve remarkable remissions in refractory B cell malignancies, yet deleterious side effects such as cytokine release syndrome (CRS) limit their broader application. Current preclinical assays on manufactured cell products do not predict human clinical function.

pmc-13053546.title: Inference of the 3D pressure field exerted by a single cell from a thin membrane transverse deformation
pmc-13053546.creator: Quentin Bédel, Loïc Dupré, Nicolas Destainville
pmc-13053546.description: AbstractNumerous cell types relate to their immediate environment by exerting a three-dimensional pressure field on their environment, with components both longitudinal and transverse to the cell membrane. This pressure field can in principle be measured by traction force microscopy experiments.

pmc-13171383.title: Epigenetic signatures and cellular stress response pathways in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a personalized medicine perspective
pmc-13171383.creator: Fabian M. Cortés-Mancera, Marianne G. Rots, Han Moshage, Johanna C. Arroyave-Ospina
pmc-13171383.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease around the world, with at least 40% global prevalence. Although genetic susceptibility contributes to disease risk, it does not fully explain the marked interindividual variability in disease onset, severity, and progression.

pmc-13231074.title: Mindfulness combined with cognitive motor dual task training in Parkinson’s disease with mild cognitive impairment
pmc-13231074.creator: Rui Wang, Jing-Zhi Zhang, Si-Mao Xu, Jun Chen, Ben-xiang He
pmc-13231074.description: SummaryParkinson’s disease with mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI) is a common non-motor manifestation that severely impairs functional independence and quality of life. A single-blind randomized controlled trial was conducted to evaluate whether mindfulness combined with cognitive-motor dual-task training (CMDT) improves multidimensional outcomes in patients with PD-MCI.

uslaw-usc-t48-s1695.title: 48 U.S.C. § 1695 — Federal education and health care programs; nonapplicability or nonparticipation
uslaw-usc-t48-s1695.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t48-s1695.description: United States Code, Title 48 (Territories And Insular Possessions); Chapter 14 (Trust Territory Of The Pacific Islands). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, except in cases in which the Federal program is terminated with respect to all recipients under the program, Federal programs in the fields of education and health care shall not cease to apply to.
